design: EdgeFHE V8b rev5 HLS kernel edgefhe_v8b, ENC (command 9), v8b_rev5/hardware/hls/v8b.cpp

label_legend.ESTIMATED: derived from the HLS source (trip counts x II from the pragmas, plus pipeline depths inferred from the routed hierarchy report) and the schedule model
label_legend.MEASURED: board numbers measured by the team (V8b rev5, 2026-11-23, k = 8): the driver phases of one call (10-run V8b comparison (2026-11-23), rep 1, last call of board_enc_check sustain 30 8) and the means of the ten 30-s V8b runs of that comparison

method: cycles = trip count x II from the pragmas (II-only lower bound) plus pipeline fill/drain and call overhead; depths are inferred from the core latencies visible in hardware/reports/rev5/hierarchical.rpt (no csynth/cosim report is in the repository); the DATAFLOW interaction is replayed by a token-level model (energy_probe/kv260/partition/hls_model/v8b_sched_model.py) with the FIFO depths of v8b.cpp:609-632

modules.name: read message (int64 in) and reduce m to 3 limbs (residue64)
modules.label: ESTIMATED

loops.note: one coefficient per iteration, one 128-bit input beat every 2 iterations, one m token per limb every 4

overlapped_with: limb engines (NTT/INTT of the previous ciphertext)
modules.comment: read and reduce are one fused loop; the m0-m2 FIFOs (depth 1024 = one polynomial) let the reader run one ciphertext ahead; in the model it is blocked ~18k cycles per ciphertext

modules.name: ChaCha20 keystream for the ternary mask u (8-block interleaved core)
modules.label: ESTIMATED

loops.note: 80 cycles for 10 double rounds of 8 blocks + 8 output cycles; TRIPCOUNT 2 batches (v8b.cpp:310)

overlapped_with: nothing inside the sampler (sequential with the byte decode)

modules.name: ternary decode, 5 trits per accepted byte (< 243)
modules.label: ESTIMATED

loops.note: II=2 because one byte can emit two 4-trit tokens to the same FIFO; the loop always runs 512 iterations

overlapped_with: 32 tokens of head start overlap the previous store p=1
modules.comment: 1024 tokens need ~864 bytes (820 accepted): batch 2 is needed up to byte ~352; the decoder makes ~0.59 tokens/cycle and the 32-deep u FIFO limits the head start to 32 tokens

modules.name: ChaCha20 keystreams for e0 and e1 (2 x 512 blocks)
modules.label: ESTIMATED

loops.note: 2 polys x 64 batches, LOOP_FLATTEN off; each batch = one 8-block chacha8 call (88-cycle core)

overlapped_with: limb NTT / pointwise / INTT of the same ciphertext (e FIFOs depth 1024 hold a whole polynomial)
modules.comment: largest single sampler item; not overlapped with CDT63 (sequential in the batch loop)

dataflow.processes: reader | sampler | limb<0> | limb<1> | limb<2> | writer (v8b.cpp:601, 645-650); every channel is an hls::stream FIFO, no ping-pong buffers

fifos.m0-m2: 1024 x 128 bit = one message polynomial per limb (URAM)
fifos.e00-e12: 1024 x 32 bit = one e polynomial per FIFO (URAM)
fifos.o0-o2: 1024 x 128 bit = one store's output per limb (URAM)

overlap_across_ciphertexts: sampler: e0(f), e1(f) are generated while the limb engines run NTT/pointwise/INTT of f (e FIFOs hold a whole polynomial)
sampler: the mask of f+1 can run only 32 tokens ahead (us FIFO depth 32); the rest of ternary(f+1) is in lockstep with u_load(f+1)
reader: m(f+1) enters while store p=0 of f drains m(f) (m FIFO = exactly one polynomial)
writer: c0(f) drains during pointwise/INTT p=1 of f; c1(f) drains during u_load(f+1) and the start of NTT(f+1)
inside a limb engine: u_load, 12 CT stages, then (pointwise, 12 GS stages, store) x 2 run strictly one after another (no DATAFLOW inside limb)

bottleneck.label: ESTIMATED
bottleneck.stage: limb engine chain: u_load (waiting for the ternary sampler) -> 12 CT stages -> [pointwise -> 12 GS stages -> store] x 2; three engines in lockstep

runner_up.note: co-critical: the sampler becomes the bottleneck when one chacha8 call costs more than ~115 cycles (372 slack cycles / 130 calls per ciphertext; model sweep)

sensitivity.grid: ct/gs stage call 551-571 cycles, chacha8 call 96-124 cycles; sweep_k8.json
sensitivity.measurement_constraint: parameter sets whose PL-only frame exceeds the MEASURED 1075.3 us (every grid point with a chacha8 call >= 120 cycles) are excluded; the partition campaign's 1074.4 us excludes the same points

predicted_us_per_frame_k8_scope: PL only: ap_start to the last output beat accepted by the S2MM; excludes DMA programming before ap_start and the IRQ/wake after completion

measured.sustained_source: mean of the ten V8b runs (104,982.4 ciphertexts in 30.0008 s)

gap.label: MEASURED minus ESTIMATED
candidates: driver work inside the dma_hls window: issue_pending of both AXI DMA channels before ap_start and the S2MM IOC interrupt -> tasklet -> callback -> thread wake (ef_v8b_main.c:315-320); not determinable from source; ns_rx_wake / ns_tx_callback (ef_v8b_main.c:366-367) isolate parts of it
S2MM below 1 beat/cycle during the final drain: 80 % -> +3.8 us, 67 % -> +7.7 us, 50 % -> +15.3 us (model)
HLS pipeline depths / call overheads above the central assumption: +5 cycles per NTT/INTT stage -> +7.2 us per frame
not steady-state DMA bandwidth: needs 0.25 GB/s in and 0.74 GB/s out on average versus 3.2 GB/s per direction (128 bit x 200 MHz)

dma.label: ESTIMATED (from block design)
dma.config: AXI DMA 7.1 simple mode, 128-bit MM and stream, MM2S burst 4 beats, S2MM burst 16 beats, all at the 200 MHz fabric clock; both channels -> axi_interconnect (2 SI, 1 MI, SAMD crossbar) -> S_AXI_HP0_FPD 128 bit
dma.mm2s_needed: no effect while MM2S >= 0.125 beat/cycle (0.40 GB/s, set by the first message); 0.10 beat/cycle -> +15 us (model, back-pressured)
dma.s2mm_needed: steady state unaffected while S2MM >= 0.33 beat/cycle (1.07 GB/s); the final drain is 2048 beats + trailer

notes: No HLS csynth or co-simulation report for V8b rev5 is in the repository (run_v8b_export.tcl writes v8b_ip_prj/, not committed); pipeline depths are inferred, not read.
II values are the pragma targets. The MEASURED 1075.3 us supports II=1 for the NTT/INTT stages: II=2 would give about 1.8 ms per k=8 frame.

Core latencies are read from module names in hierarchical.rpt (trailing number = latency + 1, consistent with BIND_OP latency 3/2/3 of mont(), v8b.cpp:44-48): ct_cycle holds urem_11ns_12ns_12_15_1 and sdiv_14ns_14ns_12_18_1 (lines 316-321), gs_cycle holds udiv_28ns_17ns_12_32_1 (lines 349-351). They come from the variable divisions of the address/twiddle index (v8b.cpp:385-387, 426-428) and add ~47 cycles of fill/drain to each of the 36 stage calls per ciphertext (~1764 cycles, 8.8 us).

chacha8: the routed hierarchy shows the key-copy and zero-state loops (v8b.cpp:136, 138) as 16 separate pipelined sub-loops (hierarchical.rpt:731-778). The central value assumes they run concurrently (~19 cycles). Run one after another (~220 cycles) the sampler would need ~52k cycles per ciphertext (~2.1 ms per frame), which the MEASURED 1075.3 us excludes.
The ternary acceptance (byte < 243) is random; batch 2 is needed up to byte ~352 +/- 7; the probability of a third batch is negligible (TRIPCOUNT 2, v8b.cpp:310).
The three limb engines are identical and fed in lockstep (the sampler writes u0/u1/u2 and e*0/e*1/e*2 in one statement), so one engine was modelled; their cycle counts are per engine, not summed.

dma_hls (ef_v8b_main.c:315-320, 368) starts before dmaengine issue_pending of RX and TX and ends when the ioctl thread wakes after the S2MM callback; the model covers ap_start to the last output beat only.

Sustained 104,982 ct in 30.0 s (MEASURED, mean of the ten V8b runs) = 3499 ct/s = 285.8 us per ciphertext = 2.286 ms per k=8 frame, which equals the measured mean ioctl (2.286 ms), i.e. the serialized ioctl; the PL is busy about 47 % of it.

The model is compared with the lowest single-call dma_hls values: 1075.3 us (the lowest of the ten V8b runs' last calls, which range 1075.3-1126.8 us) and 1074.4 us (partition campaign, sustain k = 8, last call; gap 17.5 us). dma_hls also contains driver work that varies from call to call, so the slower calls carry more software time.
Module us_per_ct values are each module's own busy time (depth-adjusted). They overlap in time, so they do not add up to the frame time; the per-ciphertext time is set by the bottleneck chain.
For a 'PL does only NTT/pointwise/INTT' partition, ntt_mask + pointwise + intt = 22274 cycles (111.4 us) per ciphertext per limb engine (ESTIMATED), without the u_load wait or the store.
